questions.q: What is an AI agent for a restaurant?
questions.a: An AI agent works like a digital employee that handles specific tasks for your restaurant. It understands what a guest or staff member is asking, finds the right information and acts on it. Depending on the setup, it can take an order, book a table, send a follow-up or flag an unhappy guest for a manager.

questions.q: What's the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?
questions.a: A simple chatbot mostly answers questions, while an AI agent can also take action. An agent can complete a reservation, place an order or route a complaint to the right person. That makes agents useful for work that used to need a staff member every time.

questions.q: What can restaurants use AI agents for?
questions.a: The most common uses are order taking, reservations, guest support and marketing. Agents can answer calls, book tables, handle everyday questions, collect feedback and help respond to reviews. Some also monitor stock levels and help managers build schedules based on expected demand.

questions.q: How do I set up an AI agent for my restaurant?
questions.a: Pick one repetitive task first, such as answering guest questions or replying to reviews, and choose a vendor that can connect the agent to your systems. Give it your menu, hours, policies and FAQs, then decide when it should hand off to a staff member. Test it with common questions before launch and keep adjusting as you learn.

questions.q: Which AI agent is best for my restaurant?
questions.a: The right choice depends on where guests reach you and what slows your team down. A busy phone line calls for voice AI, a social-first brand may want an Instagram or WhatsApp tool, and a team with developers can build a custom agent. Multi-location brands that want reviews and messages from every channel in one place can use Momos, whose AI agents reply on-brand and surface trends by location.
